text:
Alex: quick q — for the A/B canary we rolled yesterday, do we have a documented ‘get-well’/progressive-degradation pathway if the canary degrades unexpectedly?
Maria: short answer: partial. we have fallback at router level but no formalized staged degrade + recovery script.
Sam: can you clarify what you mean by "get-well"? automated mitigation + rehab of the canary? or just fallback to main variant?
Alex: both. ideally: 1) immediate safe fallback, 2) automated throttled retry/repair of canary, 3) gradual re-intro once metrics recover. want to avoid manual churn for every flaky canary.
Karen: +1. also need to consider stateful sessions & KV cache warming — we can't just cut traffic and hope cache repopulates.
Maria: noted. current router supports fallback to upstream model id; we also have traffic-slicing that can route x% to canary. but no health-driven ramp-down/up loop.
Sam: thinking out loud: health signals -> policy engine -> actions. signals: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, hallucination/regression evals, token cost. actions: immediate 0% route, throttle to 10%, pause writes/evict cache, trigger canary-restart job, notify oncall.
Alex: exactly. can we design the policy primitive minimal enough to be reused across hosted/dedicated/private? interface needs to be simple: Signal -> Predicate -> Action.
Karen: example policy (pseudo):
```json
{
  "signal":"error_rate_1m",
  "predicate":">0.02",
  "actions":["route:0%","notify:oncall","start:canary-restart"]
}
```
Maria: that’s good. but add cool-down windows and hysteresis, otherwise flappy networks will chop traffic constantly.
Sam: add these fields: min-duration, cool_down, recovery-check (what metrics to look at to re-open). e.g. recovery-check: p95<250ms for 5m.
Alex: also want a 'degraded mode' action that reduces model size/quantization variant instead of full fallback. e.g. route to canary-quantized-8bit. cheaper and preserves feature parity where possible.
Karen: but that requires runtime to support transparent variant substitution + KV cache translation. need an adapter layer. can't rely on naive fallback.
Maria: ops considerations: when policy triggers restart, must run a sequenced plan: cordon node, drain active sessions, start replacement, confirm probes, resume traffic. automated but with failsafe manual abort.
Sam: note on metrics: add synthetic prompt probes & eval-suite against golden prompts. those catch quality regressions that latency-only probes miss.
Alex: agree. probes should run from multiple regions to catch network/regional regressions.
Maria: deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.18/canary-policy-engine started by @maria  (this is a simulated bot note).
deploy-bot: build/ci 0d9a2f - canary-policy-engine image pushed to registry :package: 2390012400
Oncall Bot: FYI @Oncall — policy engine canary will begin routing at 15% at 2390012500. alerts will go to #eng-oncall.
Karen: question: what storage for policy state? etcd? postgres? prefer something consistent across Private customers.
Sam: propose storing policy defs in control-plane postgres and runtime caches in etcd/consul. policy decisions replayable from audit logs.
Alex: next steps: 1) draft minimal policy schema (Maria + Sam) 2) prototype runtime adapter (Karen) 3) add synthetic probe harness (Alex) — sync tomorrow 11am.
Maria: i'll sketch schema in repo and drop link. want lightweight DSL first, then compile to runtime actions.
Sam: also will add unit tests for hysteresis and blackbox probe failure modes.
Alex: nice. if we can automate a safe rehab loop, we'll reduce manual rollbacks 70%+ for canaries. :100:
Maria: sweet. ping me if you want early review of the schema.
Sam: thanks everyone. closing loop after the draft.
